title: Little Malvern and West Malvern Circular Walk Route

images.title: Andrew Darge / Little Malvern
images.caption: Little Malvern is also home to St Wulstan’s Roman Catholic Church, where the composer Edward Elgar and his wife are buried. The area lies within the Malvern Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and offers access to walking routes with wide views over the surrounding countryside.

description: This circular walk explores the Malvern Hills from the village of Little Malvern. There is a public car park near the village where you can start the walk. You then head north to climb into the surrounding Malvern Hills where you can enjoy some stunning views over the area. On the way you will pass Worcestershire Beacon and the nearby village of West Malvern. Little Malvern is noted for its historic priory and gardens. The most prominent landmark is Little Malvern Priory, founded as a Benedictine monastery around 1125. Although much of the complex was dismantled during the Dissolution of the Monasteries, the chancel and central tower survive, dating from a 15th century rebuilding. The priory church, dedicated to St Giles, is Grade I listed and contains notable stained glass, including its east window. Beside the priory stands Little Malvern Court, created from the former Prior’s Hall and cloisters after the Dissolution. The house has remained in the Berington family since the sixteenth century and combines medieval features with later Victorian additions. It contains historic interiors with paintings, furniture, vestments and needlework. The gardens of Little Malvern Court cover about ten acres of former monastic grounds. They include garden rooms, a water garden with a chain of lakes, mature trees, spring bulbs, and roses, all set against views across the Severn Valley. The gardens are open to the public at certain times of the year, often in spring.
